summary: At a median home price of $358,000, Cherry Valley sits in a price band that's increasingly rare anywhere in Southern California within striking distance of the San Gorgonio and San Jacinto mountain ranges — a home-price-to-income ratio of roughly 4.6, which registers as genuinely attainable compared to much of the inland empire. Spread across eight square miles at only 913 people per square mile, the area reads physically as semi-rural high desert transitioning into foothill terrain east of Beaumont, with open views toward the snow-capped peaks of the San Bernardino National Forest. The pace is unmistakably quiet; there is no downtown grid, no evening sidewalk culture, and most errands require a car. Employment skews toward a bedroom-community pattern — logistics hubs along the I-10 corridor, healthcare facilities in nearby Banning and Beaumont, and distribution centers further west toward Riverside account for most commute destinations, meaning switching jobs usually means switching drives. The climate delivers 9.8 hours of daily sunshine and mild 74°F average highs, though summer days push well past that and winter nights in the foothills can dip sharply. Cherry Valley is fundamentally a place where affordable square footage and mountain-framed horizons come packaged with distance from almost everything else.
